$comment: D4.48 — Instrument classes. What was required, what was done, the evidence, and what remains open.

Measured on 21 October 2026 against GitHub commit 223bfc821 (D4.45 to D4.47 engine, plus the frontend export-button fix) and the D4.48 working tree. The term sheet stays withdrawn. Nothing here is an advocate's decision: every new clause, the classification itself and the succession records are draft-needs-legal-review.
review_status: engineering — the classification and the three new clauses await advocate review
reported_by_the_owner: Many templates are the wrong kind of document: the term sheet and the privacy policy look like agreements. 'Firstly we have to strengthen our core.'
owner_decisions_21_oct: Build the classification and fix the 29 types that generate. The 11 types that do not generate are classified but stay blocked until the advocate decides their constraint scopes.
Render the term sheet as a summary-of-terms table.
Policies carry a brief governing-law line and the routes by which a person can complain; no arbitration, indemnity, waiver or severability.

items.requirement: Every document type is drafted as the kind of instrument it is, decided in one place.
items.found: Every layer assumed a bilateral contract: blueprints listed contract general provisions; drafting_policies.json supplied thirteen by default; doctrineInjector.js added an Indian Contract Act warranty by 'the Parties' to every document; the commercial engine and the dependency resolver added indemnity, liability limits and arbitration; the identity renderer opened every instrument 'THIS AGREEMENT ("Agreement")'. The Privacy Policy called itself 'this Agreement' 28 times; the Refund and Shipping policies sent consumers to arbitration 'between the Parties'; the MOU and the Partnership Deed opened as agreements; the term sheet was laid out as a deed.
done: knowledge-base/metadata/instrument_classes.json: eight classes (AGREEMENT, NON_BINDING_TERMS, STANDARD_TERMS, PUBLISHED_POLICY, UNILATERAL_INSTRUMENT, SWORN_STATEMENT, LETTER, NOTICE), each with its contract-doctrine flag, clause rule, layout and signing form; every registered type classified, with a self-name where it has one.

backend/services/instrumentClass.js is the only reader. The doctrine injector, the hardening baseline, the identity opening, the instrument noun and validation ask it; the last generation stage (finaliseSurvivalReferences) removes any clause the class forbids, whichever stage added it, and records what it removed on draft.metadata.instrument_class.
shared/documentShape.js reads its coarse shapes from the same file, so the checks and the assembly cannot disagree; the mapping is unchanged for all 44 classified types and for an unknown one.

Only AGREEMENT, NON_BINDING_TERMS, STANDARD_TERMS and PUBLISHED_POLICY are enforced. The four classes of the 11 non-generating types are recorded but not applied, so their reasons for refusal do not move before the advocate decides them (the PoSH Policy is held out by name).
A type name is canonicalised before lookup ('privacy_policy' was found to fall through to AGREEMENT; fixed).

items.requirement: A published policy carries none of an agreement's general provisions, states its governing law briefly, and tells the reader how to complain.
done: Privacy Policy blueprint 4.0: CORE_DEFINITIONS, CORE_DATA_PROCESSING, CORE_COMPLIANCE_WITH_LAW, CORE_LIMITATION_LIABILITY, CORE_DISPUTE_RESOLUTION, CORE_GOVERNING_LAW and the optional entire-agreement clause removed; PRIVACY_SECURITY_SHARING_001 (DPDP Act s.8(2), 8(5), 8(6), 16) and PRIVACY_LAW_AND_COMPLAINTS_001 (withdrawal of consent s.6(4), 6(6); complaint to the Board s.13(3); notice content s.5(1); a one-sentence governing law) added.
Refund and Shipping blueprints: CORE_GOVERNING_LAW_001, which pulled in arbitration through required_with, replaced by ECOM_POLICY_GOVERNING_LAW_001 (Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.100 and s.2(46)).
PRIVACY_SIGNATURE_BLOCK_001: 'and agree to be bound by' removed; consent under DPDP s.6 is purpose-specific, not inferred from use.
The intake no longer asks the three policies for a governing-law state, and the governing-law-state consistency check applies only where a governing-law clause exists.
items.result: All three generate in every fixture world with no CORE_ or AUTO- clause, no warranty, no arbitration, never 'this Agreement' or 'the Parties', and pass the export gate with nothing blocking.

items.priority: P0 (found in this phase; would have shipped)
items.requirement: A document a user saved before a template changed can still be downloaded (the D4.47 rule: never refuse for a finding the user did not cause and cannot act on).
items.found: As first written, the new policy blueprints require clauses an old policy does not have. The engine reports a missing required clause as CRITICAL, so every Privacy, Refund and Shipping policy saved before D4.48 — each shown 'Automated checks passed' at 100 — was refused at export. The conservation gate cannot see this: its corpus is freshly generated documents.
done: Each changed blueprint records its succession: the new clause and the clauses it replaced.

backend/services/clauseSuccession.js re-scopes a missing required clause to SUPERSEDED_TEMPLATE_CLAUSE (Requires legal review, 'generate the document again') only when the document still carries a clause the new one replaced. A current document missing a required clause with nothing it replaced is still blocked.
IRE blueprintValidator.js: the finding names its clause as data (missing_clause_id), so nothing parses the message.
The validation layer instrument_class reports each provision a saved document's class forbids, and the Contract Act warranty, as Requires legal review; it never blocks.
items.frozen_evidence: tests/fixtures/savedBeforeInstrumentClasses.D4_48.json (Privacy, Refund, Shipping and ToS as generated and saved at 223bfc821)
items.result: All four saved documents export; each now shows Requires legal review instead of 'Automated checks passed'. That is a change of outcome for saved documents and it is deliberate: each still contains the contract provisions that were the defect.

done: Terms of Service (STANDARD_TERMS): no longer carries the warranty that 'the Parties' gave free consent and are competent to contract; keeps its limitation of liability, indemnity and forum clauses, which a standard-form contract may carry.
Partnership Deed opens 'THIS DEED OF PARTNERSHIP ("Deed")' and calls itself 'this Deed'; MOU opens 'THIS MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ("MOU")'. The definition follows the noun.

Found by the conservation gate: the Deed's indemnity ('breach of this Deed') then failed the indemnity-scope matcher, which accepted only 'breach of this agreement' — a false finding and 20 points off every Partnership Deed. The matcher now accepts every self-name the model declares.

items.requirement: The term sheet is presented as a summary of terms, not as a deed, in every export format.
done: backend/services/exportService.js: a type whose class has layout 'terms_table' prints its parties and recitals as before, then a table — Term, Status, Proposed terms — then the execution block. Status is the family's declared provision_status (Binding / Non-binding / Not yet determined), the same declaration the coherence checks enforce. Clause text is verbatim, with the usual decimal numbering.

DOCX: a real table with a header row repeated on every page. PDF: drawn by hand (pdfkit has no table); a row that runs over a page continues under a repeated header, marked '(continued)', and keeps its opening lines with the term. TXT: one block per row with the term and its status on the heading line; the clause text is not wrapped, because wrapping it into a fixed-width grid would split its sentences.
A superseded term sheet keeps the layout it was generated with: D4.44 exports it unchanged.
items.checked_by_eye: PDF and DOCX rendered to images and inspected (column widths widened after 'Non-binding' was found wrapping).
items.verified_by: tests/instrumentClasses.test.mjs §9; termSheetFalsification and termSheetWithdrawal unchanged and passing

measurements.conservation_gate: Re-baselined and explained in provenance-instrumentation.json → the_gate.rebaselines (2026-10-21).
measurements.frontend_build: vite build passes (documentShape.js now reads JSON through createRequire; no frontend module imports it).

still_open: Advocate review: the classification itself; PRIVACY_SECURITY_SHARING_001, PRIVACY_LAW_AND_COMPLAINTS_001 and ECOM_POLICY_GOVERNING_LAW_001 and their citations (which DPDP provisions and rules are in force on a policy's effective date; Consumer Protection Act s.100 and s.2(46)). They raise the unreviewed clause count from 313 to 316 (clauseProvenance, already over its ceiling of 307; the ceiling was not raised).

tosFalsification (a known failing suite) now fails earlier: D4.48 removed two of the four self-certifying claims it documents (free consent, capacity). Its evidence must be re-gathered against the current ToS, as the test itself says; not done here, to keep workstreams separate.
The ToS still calls itself 'this Agreement'; 'these Terms' needs plural handling in the noun swap.
The MOU recital asserts the Parties intend a legally binding arrangement, whatever the user chose (advocate question: MOU binding classification).
Policies still ask agreement questions such as cure period, non-compete and the second party's signatory (intake workstream).
A saved Privacy Policy shows one INSTRUMENT_CLASS_MISMATCH per contract provision (10 findings). Accurate, but noisy; grouping them is a presentation decision.
The 11 non-generating types: classified, not enforced, awaiting the advocate's constraint-scope decisions.
Restoring the term sheet still requires an advocate's APPROVED with a name and a date; the table changes its presentation, not its status.
